To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the performance of truck trips is the main driver of the adoption of technologies that reduce fuel use and GHG emissions, 2) the adoption of these technologies can be incentivized through the adoption of policies that reduce the time spent in transit, and 3) the effect of policies that reduce transit times can be amplified by the discounting of future costs by firms.
“improving the performance of truck fleets (speeding up the shipments) could reduce GHG emissions significantly, by incentivizing investments in technologies that reduce fuel consumption.”
